payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the woman's jacket fully closed, with its front panels together and no visible opening remaining along the closure?
node.criteria: Pass: the jacket is visibly fully closed, with its front panels together and no opening along the closure. Fail: the jacket is visibly not fully closed, including any visible opening along the closure. Unknown: the closure or its full extent cannot be judged from the image.
node.binding: Directly inspect the requested endpoint in the edited image; the input image is context for identifying the woman's jacket, not a prerequisite for checking the endpoint.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the woman's jacket hanging open, with a clear gap between the front panels.
The edited image shows the jacket hanging open, with a clear gap between its front panels.
The jacket is visibly open in the edited image, with its front panels separated and a large opening remaining.

fulfillment: The node’s binding and criteria already express the requested endpoint and the partial-progress distinction; the repeated traces consistently report the jacket open with no visible progress, so they do not reveal a binding or evidence failure. However, the supplied edited image appears to show the woman turned sideways with the pink jacket hanging open, which supports “not fully closed”; the source also appears open, so the no-progress finding is plausible. This conflicts with the aggregate reference label “yes,” but that label constrains only the overall result and is not atomic ground truth. Do not change the visual criterion or force a yes. Investigate whether the reference label, image pairing, or upstream support-node outputs are misaligned with this example; keep endpoint and progress judgments separate, and preserve unknown when the relevant visual evidence is genuinely insufficient. The traces are valid, queried, and high-confidence, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated.
s2: The node’s endpoint, comparison binding, and partial-progress criterion are already appropriate; do not alter them to force agreement with the aggregate “yes.” The images show a substantial pose change: in the source the woman faces forward and the jacket front appears together/closed or nearly closed, while in the edit she is turned sideways and the pink jacket hangs open. The traces’ repeated “open in both images/no progress” conclusion may therefore reflect a comparison or garment-orientation error, not evidence that the requested closure progressed. Re-examine the same jacket’s front and closure cues across the two views, distinguishing a changed pose or occlusion from actual closure; retain unknown if the comparison cannot establish direction. Also verify the image pairing and upstream s1 result against the images, since its high-confidence “open” assessment may be misbound or mistaken. The traces are valid and queried, so this is not a transport/schema failure; the reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth.

response.content: {"text":"The endpoint criterion is appropriately strict, but the binding is too one-sided: it explicitly treats the source only as context and asks only whether the edited jacket is fully closed. That can detect completion, but cannot distinguish no progress from partial progress when the edit remains open. Bind the check to the same jacket and closure cues in both images, comparing their visible state while accounting for the changed pose and possible occlusion; report progress only when the comparison supports it, and retain unknown if direction cannot be judged. Here the source appears to show the front together or nearly closed, while the edited view is turned sideways and the jacket hangs open, so the repeated high-confidence “open” observations do not establish that no change occurred. Investigate the image pairing and the visual interpretation of the closure rather than weakening the full-closure requirement or forcing the aggregate reference “yes,” which is not atomic ground truth. Traces are valid and queried; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
